title: herbstutil
description: A stdin filter that turns the verbose output of herbstclient attr into clean JSON - for scripting the herbstluftwm tiling window manager.

content.heading: herbstutil - JSON bridge to herbstluftwm
content: herbstutil is a small command-line filter that post-processes the output of `herbstclient attr` into clean JSON - so the state of the herbstluftwm window manager can be consumed wherever JSON is spoken.
[https://github.com/akinevz2/herbstutil](https://github.com/akinevz2/herbstutil)

content.heading: herbstluftwm in a nutshell
content: herbstluftwm is a manual tiling window manager for Linux. Its core idea: the whole desktop is one global object tree - monitors, tags, clients (windows), settings - queried and modified over IPC with the companion tool herbstclient.
The tree is probed with `herbstclient attr <path>`: it prints a short description of the node, its children, and a table of every attribute (typed, writable, hookable).

```sh
$ herbstclient attr clients.            # children of the clients node
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus.      # introspect the focused window
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus.tag   # read a single leaf value
```
The catch: `attr` output is written for humans first - padded type tables, prose, legends. Great to read, fragile to parse.

content.heading: What herbstutil does
content: herbstutil reads `herbstclient attr` output on stdin and rebuilds it as JSON, preserving the node's shape:
value - the node's description; children - the names of the child nodes; attributes - every attribute as a name-value pair.
Where herbstclient speaks humans, herbstutil speaks machine.

content.heading: Usage
content: herbstutil is a stdin filter built with Bun and bunli, packaged as a single executable:

```sh
$ herbstclient attr clients. | herbstutil
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus. | herbstutil --space 2
```
s, --space <n> - pretty-print with `n` spaces of indentation (default 4)
It refuses to run attached to a terminal: herbstutil always reads from stdin.

content.heading: Examples
content: The same node, before and after `| herbstutil`.

content.heading: Root node: herbstclient attr clients.
content: Raw:

```text
$ herbstclient attr clients.
The managed windows. For every (managed) window id there is an entry here.

5 children:
  0x400003.
  0x700003.
  0xc00003.
  0xe80003.
  focus.
0 attributes.
 .---- type
 | .-- writable
 | | .-- hookable
 V V V
```
Piped through herbstutil:

content.heading: Node with attributes: herbstclient attr clients.focus.
content: Raw (excerpt):

```text
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus.
a managed window

1 child:
  parent_frame.
24 attributes:
 s - - class = "Alacritty"
 b w h decorated = true
 b w h floating = false
 i - h pid = 61763
 s - h tag = "work"
 s - h title = "OC | Customizing opencode and dotfiles"
 b - h visible = true
```
Piped through herbstutil (excerpt - all 24 attributes arrive in the JSON):

```json
{
    "value": "a managed window",
    "children": [
        "parent_frame."
    ],
    "attributes": {
        "class": "\"Alacritty\"",
        "decorated": "true",
        "floating": "false",
        "pid": "61763",
        "tag": "\"work\"",
        "title": "\"OC | Customizing opencode and dotfiles\"",
        "urgent": "false",
        "visible": "true",
        "winid": "\"0x700003\""
    }
}
```
Note how attribute values stay as raw strings - a reminder that everything coming from `attr` is text until you parse it downstream.

content.heading: Leaf node: herbstclient attr clients.focus.tag
content: Raw:

```text
$ herbstclient attr clients.focus.tag
work
```
